newsitem.title: INDIA: India policeman in bribe trap after winning medal.
newsitem.headline: India policeman in bribe trap after winning medal.

text.p: An Indian policeman who won a medal for meritorious conduct was trapped while accepting a bribe of 50,000 rupees ($1,400) the very next day, a police statement said.

Police in India's financial capital said they caught Inspector Layakmiya Shaikh red-handed on Saturday, soon after he received the President's Medal for meritorious service on August 15, the golden jubilee of India's independence from Britain.
Ironically, India had marked its 50th anniversary with a vow to stamp out corruption.
Shaikh demanded the money as the first instalment of a 500,000-rupee bribe to refrain from arresting a shipping company executive involved in a dispute over dock charges, the statement said.
"Shaikh was trapped while demanding and accepting the bribe amount of 50,000 rupees as the first instalment," it said, adding that he had been arrested.
"Shaikh has been awarded the President's Medal for meritorious service on August 15, 1997," the statement said.
The President's Medal is one of the highest honours an Indian policeman can achieve.
